nodes.summary: For a Brownian motion `B` with continuous paths and measurable coordinates and `t > 0`, `S_t = sup_{s ≤ t} B s` has the same law as `|B_t|` (Le Gall, ENS notes *Intégration, Probabilités et Processus Aléatoires*, Théorème 14.5.2, second assertion).
nodes.title: The running maximum has the law of `|B_t|`

nodes.summary: For a Brownian motion `B` with continuous paths and `a > 0`, the hitting time `T_a = inf {t ≥ 0 : B t = a}` has the density `a / √(2π s³) · exp(-a² / (2s))` on `(0, ∞)`; equivalently, since `T_a ≤ t` exactly when the path reaches `a` on `[0, t]`, `P(T_a ≤ t) = ∫_0^t a / √(2π s³) · exp(-a² / (2s)) ds` for every `t ≥ 0` (Le Gall, ENS notes *Intégration, Probabilités et Processus Aléatoires*, Corollaire 14.5.3).
nodes.title: Law of the hitting time of a level

nodes.summary: For a Brownian motion `B` with continuous paths, `S_t = sup_{s ≤ t} B s`, `t > 0`, `a ≥ 0` and `b ≤ a`, `P(S_t ≥ a, B_t ≤ b) = P(B_t ≥ 2a - b)` (Le Gall, ENS notes *Intégration, Probabilités et Processus Aléatoires*, Théorème 14.5.2, proved by applying the strong Markov property at the hitting time of `a`).
nodes.title: Reflection principle

nodes.summary: Let `B` be a Brownian motion with continuous paths and measurable coordinates, and `T` a stopping time of its natural filtration with `P(T < ∞) > 0`. Conditionally on `{T < ∞}`, the process `B^{(T)}_t = B_{T + t} - B_T` is a Brownian motion independent of the σ-algebra `F_T` of events prior to `T` (Le Gall, ENS notes *Intégration, Probabilités et Processus Aléatoires*, Théorème 14.5.1; Le Gall, GTM 274, Chapter 2,…
nodes.title: Strong Markov property of Brownian motion
